subject: an iron longsword inventory item icon for an ARPG loot grid
bestPrompt: Stylized hand-painted ARPG inventory loot icon of an iron longsword, single hero object angled diagonally about 35 degrees, blade tip toward upper-right, scaled large to fill the square icon cell. Bold painterly digital illustration in the exact flat, saturated, high-contrast finish of Diablo IV and Path of Exile 2 inventory icons — confident visible brushwork, punchy stylized rendering, deliberate hand-crafted icon look, absolutely NOT a neutral photoreal 3D product render. Forged iron blade with a clearly defined central ridge and fuller, hand-painted brushed-steel highlights, one bright cool-white specular edge highlight, deep dark core shadow, warm bounce light on the underside, hammer-forge dimpling, temper mottling and worn battle nicks. Aged brown wrapped-leather grip with distinct individual painted coils, dark iron crossguard and an engraved beveled disc pommel. Strong punchy warm-and-cool rim light making the whole sword pop with high light-to-dark contrast, cleanly separated from a simple dark neutral charcoal radial-vignette background. Crisp readable silhouette, rich material rendering, high detail, high contrast, saturated. No text, no watermark, no letters, no border, no UI, no colored fog haze, no glow halo, no low-poly, no muddy midtones, no photographic backdrop.
technique: The dominant lever is forcing FLAT / SATURATED / HIGH-CONTRAST PAINTERLY illustration with explicit anti-photoreal negatives ('confident visible brushwork', 'absolutely NOT a neutral photoreal 3D product render'). Leonardo defaults to a matte low-poly or stock-render look; naming the anchor games (D4/PoE2) plus 'hand-painted' and 'visible brushwork' is what moved styleCohesion from 44 to ~78. Second lever: an explicit lighting recipe — one bright cool-white specular edge highlight + deep dark core shadow + warm bounce + punchy warm/cool rim light 'cleanly separated from a dark charcoal radial-vignette' — which builds the deliberate value hierarchy (47 to 78) that flat placeholder icons lack. Third: itemize the weak zones the judge names (distinct painted leather coils, engraved beveled pommel, defined ridge/fuller) so material rendering reads crafted, not stochastic. Note: avoid over-stacking the word 'crisp/sharp' — it tips the model back toward a photoreal render and merges the item into the vignette (that regression cost ~16 points).

iterations.note: Painterly D4/PoE2 hero framing + full lighting recipe + forged-steel material + anti-text/border negatives. Material jumped 40->80, but read as a photographic 3D render on a vertical axis that wasted the square cell.
Added 'hand-painted / visible brushwork' anti-photoreal push and a 45-degree diagonal filling the cell. StyleCohesion rose to 70; docked for a teal-fog gen-fill background and soft AI-mush edges.

Reverted to near-vertical and over-emphasized 'crisp/razor-sharp' per judge fix. Regression: over-crisping tipped it back to neutral photoreal, item merged into brown vignette, style crashed to 45. Reverted this lever.

Winner. Flat/saturated/high-contrast painterly + punchy warm-and-cool rim light + strong value separation from a neutral charcoal radial vignette + itemized weak zones (leather coils, engraved pommel). Best value hierarchy (78) and cohesion (75).
